oh_central_ohio.blurb: Central Ohio's climbing is scattered across flat farmland and parks around Columbus, which serves as the regional hub. Bouldering is about three quarters of it, with problems from V0 up to around V8, most of them easy to moderate. Roped climbing is mostly sport, from roughly 5.9 to 5.12 with the heaviest concentration at 5.10 to 5.12, and only a little trad. Marne Road is the biggest single crag, a sandstone cliff mixing sport, trad and boulders, with rock that ranges from solid to crumbly and roped climbs about 25 to 65 feet tall. Seepage keeps many cracks wet into early summer, so winter and spring days can be hit or miss. Flat Rocks, near Lancaster, is a boulder-focused park with problems from V0 to V8.

tx_enchanted_rock_state_natural_area.blurb: Enchanted Rock is a huge pink granite dome in the Llano Uplift of central Texas, north of Fredericksburg, rising roughly 425 feet above the surrounding country inside a state natural area. Climbing here is mainly traditional, with cracks protected by removable gear, and many of the bolted routes are more sporty than sport, with long runouts between anchors. Bouldering is a big part of the mix too, with plenty of easy problems and a hard tail up to around V11. Roped grades run from about 5.4 to 5.13, centered on 5.9 to 5.11. Main Dome, Little Dome and Echo Canyon are the biggest sub-areas, and many anchors suit multi-pitch climbs, finishing with a walk-off or a rappel from stations.

nv_kyle_canyon.blurb: Kyle Canyon is one of the two main climbing zones on Mount Charleston, northwest of Las Vegas, reached by a highway that climbs to about 7,200 feet. It is almost entirely sport climbing on limestone, from layered rock threaded with chert to overhung yellow and gray walls with chunky edges. Grades run from about 5.5 to 5.14, but the bulk of it lies between 5.10 and 5.12, so it suits strong intermediates best. Rock quality varies and some of it is sharp or loose, so a helmet is wise. Cathedral Rock, The Hood, Imagination Wall and Echo Cliffs are among the larger sub-areas. The elevation gives welcome relief from Las Vegas summer heat, making summer and fall the usual seasons, while winters are cold and snowy.

il_the_holy_boulders.blurb: The Holy Boulders sit in Jackson County in southern Illinois, on the western slopes of Shawnee National Forest, not far from Alto Pass. The boulders and a cliffline are sandstone, in a shaded forest setting, and the friction is often likened to Fontainebleau. Nearly everything is bouldering, from V0 up to V13, with most problems in the V1 to V6 range and a few trad lines on the cliffline. The climbing is divided among many small zones, including The Sinkhole, Public Enemy Area and Brown Cow Area. October to early April is the recommended window, while humid summers bring poison ivy, ticks and chiggers; spring and fall are also pleasant for avoiding the heat.

ca_hidden_valley_campground.blurb: This corner of Joshua Tree National Park sits at about 4,200 feet in the desert and is a bouldering and short-trad playground with almost no approach. Bouldering and trad split the climbs roughly evenly, with a few top-ropes and sport routes. Problems run from easy to V10, mostly in the lower grades, and the roped lines go from about 5.3 to 5.13, with most between 5.8 and 5.11. The style leans on stemming, palming, overhanging arêtes and big moves on thin dikes. The Hidden Valley bouldering circuit and the Manx and Asteroid Belt circuit hold the most climbs, while Intersection Rock is a landmark with more than 40 routes, and The Blob and The Old Woman add more rock nearby.

ca_alabama_hills_north.blurb: Alabama Hills North covers the climbing north of Whitney Portal Road, near Lone Pine in the Eastern Sierra, at about 4,800 feet and reached from Movie Road. The hills form a high-desert expanse of orange-brown granitic towers and outcrops below the High Sierra and Mount Whitney, and many climbs are only a short walk from the car. Sport climbing dominates, with a substantial trad component and a few top-ropes. Grades run mostly from 5.6 to 5.11, with 5.10 the biggest group. Rock quality varies, since north-facing walls often have good patina while other rock can be loose. Cattle Pocket and Corridors, Western Wall and Paul's Paradise are among the larger sub-areas.
